beats.focal: Say the wrong thing — or say too much — and you could be handing a prosecutor the evidence they need.

beats.focal: Say these four lines, and you stay in control.

beats.focal: Most people lose their rights during traffic stops not because they're guilty, but because they don't know what to say — and they talk too much in a moment where every word becomes evidence.

beats.focal: Line one: I do not consent to any searches.

beats.focal: Line two: Am I being detained, or am I free to go?

beats.focal: Line three: I am exercising my right to remain silent.

beats.sentence: Court is.

beats.focal: Your job during a traffic stop is not to prove your innocence — it's to preserve your ability to fight later.
beats.sentence: Your job during a traffic stop is not to prove your innocence — it's to preserve your ability to fight later.
Your job during a traffic stop is not to prove your innocence — it's to preserve your ability to fight later.

beats.focal: Police can legally lie to you about evidence.
beats.sentence: Police can legally lie to you about evidence.
Police can legally lie to you about evidence.

beats.focal: They can claim your friend is in the next room confessing.
beats.sentence: They can claim your friend is in the next room confessing.
They can claim your friend is in the next room confessing.

beats.focal: They can say they already have fingerprints.
beats.sentence: They can say they already have fingerprints.
They can say they already have fingerprints.

beats.focal: None of it has to be true.
beats.sentence: None of it has to be true.

beats.focal: The only defense is to say nothing that depends on what they tell you.
beats.sentence: The only defense is to say nothing that depends on what they tell you.
The only defense is to say nothing that depends on what they tell you.

beats.focal: And here's the part most people miss: you must verbally invoke your rights.
beats.sentence: And here's the part most people miss: you must verbally invoke your rights.
And here's the part most people miss: you must verbally invoke your rights.

beats.focal: The Supreme Court held in Salinas v. Texas that silence alone can be used against you.
beats.sentence: The Supreme Court held in Salinas v. Texas that silence alone can be used against you.
The Supreme Court held in Salinas v. Texas that silence alone can be used against you.

beats.focal: You have to say the words.
beats.sentence: You have to say the words.
Out loud.
Clearly.
Every time.
Four lines.
Memorize them.
Practice them.
